question_text: A developer team wants an AI assistant embedded in their IDE that provides code suggestions, explains code, and generates unit tests for their GenAI application. Which AWS service addresses this?

options.text: Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer
Amazon Q Developer
AWS CloudShell
Amazon SageMaker Studio

explanation: Skill 2.5.4 explicitly cites Amazon Q Developer for generating and refactoring code, code suggestions for API assistance, AI component testing, and performance optimisation. Amazon Q Developer integrates into VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and the AWS Console. CodeGuru Reviewer performs static code analysis for security/quality — not interactive generation. CloudShell is a browser-based CLI environment. SageMaker Studio is an ML development environment.

question_text: A front-end developer wants to build a web interface for a GenAI chatbot using declarative UI components without writing complex WebSocket or streaming API code. Which AWS service accelerates this?

options.text: Amazon EC2 with a custom Node.js WebSocket server
AWS Amplify with AI kit components that abstract FM streaming and conversation management
Amazon Lightsail static website hosting
Amazon S3 static website hosting with CloudFront

explanation: Skill 2.5.2 cites AWS Amplify for developing declarative UI components for AI interfaces. Amplify's AI kit includes pre-built React/Vue components for conversational AI, streaming responses, and FM interaction — abstracting the underlying Bedrock API complexity. A custom EC2 WebSocket server requires significant boilerplate. Lightsail and S3/CloudFront static hosting serve files but provide no AI-specific UI components.
source_topic: AWS Amplify, GenAI UI, conversational interfaces

question_text: A company wants to automate extraction of structured data from unstructured documents at scale — invoices, contracts, and reports — using GenAI without building a custom pipeline. Which service enables this?

options.text: Amazon Textract alone
Amazon Bedrock Data Automation
Amazon Comprehend Medical
AWS Glue DataBrew

explanation: Skill 2.5.3 cites Amazon Bedrock Data Automation for automated data processing workflows. Bedrock Data Automation uses FMs to intelligently extract, classify, and summarise data from documents, images, audio, and video at scale — going beyond Textract's fixed-template extraction. Textract extracts text/tables from structured layouts but lacks semantic understanding for unstructured contracts. Comprehend Medical is healthcare NLP specifically. Glue DataBrew is a data preparation tool for structured datasets.

topic: CloudWatch Logs Insights for FM debugging
question_text: A developer needs to analyse the prompts and responses that led to a spike in poor-quality FM outputs over the past 24 hours. Which tool should they use?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to query structured log records of prompts and responses
Amazon Inspector to scan logs for vulnerabilities
AWS Config to review resource changes during the spike
Amazon Athena to query S3 access logs

explanation: Skill 2.5.6 explicitly cites CloudWatch Logs Insights for analysing prompts and responses to improve troubleshooting efficiency. With Bedrock Model Invocation Logging enabled, prompts and responses are logged to CloudWatch Logs, enabling Logs Insights queries to filter by time window, response quality signals, and error codes. Inspector is a security scanner. AWS Config tracks configuration changes — not FM I/O logs. Athena queries S3 files — useful if logs are archived to S3, but CloudWatch Logs Insights is the real-time first step.
source_topic: CloudWatch Logs Insights, Bedrock Model Invocation Logs

question_text: A business analyst without coding experience wants to build a multi-step GenAI workflow that chains several FM calls together to process customer feedback. Which Bedrock feature supports this without writing code?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows — a visual, no-code workflow builder for FM prompt chaining
AWS Lambda layers for shared GenAI logic
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines
AWS Step Functions Express Workflows

explanation: Skill 2.5.2 cites Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows as a no-code workflow builder. Prompt Flows provides a visual drag-and-drop interface for creating FM prompt chains, conditional branching, and integrating tools — requiring no code. Lambda layers share code between Lambda functions — requires programming. SageMaker Pipelines is for ML training workflows. Step Functions can orchestrate Bedrock calls but requires JSON/YAML definitions.
source_topic: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows, no-code GenAI

question_text: A company is building a new GenAI-powered API and wants its interface contract defined before any implementation begins, ensuring all consumers have a consistent expectation. Which approach supports this?

options.text: Implement the API first, then generate documentation from the code
Define the API contract first with an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification, then import it into API Gateway and implement Lambda handlers
Share the Lambda function ARN directly with consumers
Use Amazon EventBridge schema registry as the primary API contract

explanation: Skill 2.5.2 cites OpenAPI specifications for API-first development approaches. Defining the OpenAPI spec first allows consumers to generate client SDKs, write integration tests, and develop in parallel — before any backend implementation exists. API Gateway can import the OpenAPI spec directly to create routes, validation, and documentation. Code-first documentation risks inconsistency. Sharing Lambda ARNs is an internal implementation detail, not a consumer-facing contract. EventBridge schema registry is for event schemas, not request/response API contracts.
source_topic: OpenAPI specification, API-first development, API Gateway

topic: Q Business vs Bedrock Knowledge Bases
question_text: A company wants internal staff (HR, Sales, Finance) to search company documents using natural-language queries, with the search results strictly limited by each user's existing SharePoint permissions. They need minimal development effort and no custom UI code. Which solution is most appropriate?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a custom Lambda access-control layer
Amazon Q Business — managed enterprise RAG with built-in ACL inheritance from connected data sources
Amazon Kendra with a custom post-processing Lambda for access control
Build a custom RAG application using LangChain and Bedrock

explanation: Amazon Q Business (Skill 2.5.2, accessible AI interfaces) is a fully managed enterprise RAG service that inherits access control lists (ACL) directly from connected data sources like SharePoint — users only see documents they already have permission to access, enforced automatically. It provides a built-in web experience with no custom UI code needed. Bedrock Knowledge Bases (A) provides flexible RAG but requires building a custom access-control layer. Kendra (C) is being closed to new customers (July 2026). Custom LangChain (D) maximises flexibility but is the highest-effort option — opposite of minimal development.
source_topic: Amazon Q Business, ACL, managed enterprise RAG

topic: Q Business Plugins for write actions
question_text: A company uses Amazon Q Business for internal employee support. Employees want to not just find answers but also create Jira tickets directly from the chat interface without leaving Q Business. Which Q Business feature enables write actions to external systems?

options.text: Q Business Data Connectors — extend them to write back to Jira
Q Business Plugins — pre-built enterprise connectors (Jira, ServiceNow, Salesforce) that enable write actions
Amazon Bedrock Agents action groups connected to Q Business
Q Business cannot take write actions — it is read-only

explanation: Q Business Plugins are pre-built enterprise connectors (Jira, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Zendesk) that enable write actions directly from the chat interface. Data Connectors (A) are read-only ingestion connectors — they index documents but cannot write back to source systems. Bedrock Agents action groups are a different product not embedded in Q Business. Q Business supports write actions via Plugins — it is not read-only.
source_topic: Amazon Q Business Plugins, enterprise write actions

topic: SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for audit
question_text: A regulated financial services firm needs to audit their ML pipeline to trace which training dataset version produced a given deployed model endpoint. Which SageMaker capability provides this end-to-end lineage tracking?

options.text: SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking — automatically tracks relationships between datasets, training jobs, models, and endpoints; queryable via the LineageQuery API
SageMaker Model Monitor — detects data drift in production traffic
SageMaker Clarify — explains model predictions with SHAP values
SageMaker Ground Truth — labels training data

explanation: SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking creates and stores a graph of ML workflow entities (datasets, training jobs, models, endpoints) and their associations. The LineageQuery API lets you trace forward and backward through this graph — e.g. find all endpoints using a specific dataset. Model Monitor detects data drift, Clarify explains predictions, and Ground Truth labels data; none of these provide lineage tracking.
source_topic: SageMaker Lineage Tracking, ML audit, LineageQuery API

topic: SageMaker Ground Truth — training data labeling
question_text: A company is building a custom image classification model and needs to label 50,000 images efficiently. They want a managed AWS service that combines automated pre-labeling with a human review workflow. Which service is purpose-built for this?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth — provides automated labeling and a managed workforce (Mechanical Turk, private, or vendor) for human review
Amazon Rekognition — automatically labels images without human review
Amazon Textract — extracts text from images
Amazon A2I — routes already-labeled data for human review only

explanation: SageMaker Ground Truth is AWS's managed data labeling service. It uses automated pre-labeling to label high-confidence examples and routes uncertain examples to a human workforce (Amazon Mechanical Turk, private team, or AWS-managed vendors). Rekognition performs inference but does not build training datasets through human labeling pipelines. Textract extracts text. A2I is for augmenting model predictions with human review — not for building initial training label sets.
source_topic: SageMaker Ground Truth, training data labeling, HITL

question_text: A data science team wants a centralized, reusable repository for ML features that supports both real-time (online) lookups for inference and batch (offline) access for training. Which AWS service provides this?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store — provides an online store (low-latency lookup) and offline store (S3-backed for batch training), with feature versioning and sharing
Amazon DynamoDB — a NoSQL database with no ML-specific feature management
Amazon Redshift — a data warehouse for analytical SQL queries only
Amazon ElastiCache — an in-memory cache for general application data

explanation: SageMaker Feature Store is purpose-built for ML feature management. It has an online store (low-latency reads for real-time inference) and an offline store (S3-backed for batch training access) in a single managed service, with feature group versioning. DynamoDB is a general NoSQL database with no feature lineage or dual-store design. Redshift is an analytical warehouse. ElastiCache is a general-purpose cache.
source_topic: SageMaker Feature Store, online/offline store, feature engineering

topic: SageMaker Unified Studio — integrated lakehouse workspace
question_text: A cross-functional team of data engineers, data scientists, and ML engineers wants a single web-based workspace where they can access Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Q, QuickSight dashboards, and SageMaker notebooks without switching between consoles. Which service provides this unified experience?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio — a single interface integrating data, analytics, ML, and AI services including Bedrock and Q
AWS Management Console — the general AWS console, not a unified data/ML workspace
Amazon QuickSight — a BI tool, not a multi-service developer workspace
AWS Cloud9 — a cloud-based code editor, not an ML/data lakehouse workspace

explanation: SageMaker Unified Studio is a web application that brings together Bedrock, Amazon Q, QuickSight, SageMaker notebooks, and data lakehouse capabilities into one interface, enabling full-stack data and AI workflows. The AWS console is a general management UI. QuickSight is BI only. Cloud9 is a code editor.
source_topic: SageMaker Unified Studio, integrated workspace, lakehouse

topic: Amazon Q Apps — low-code GenAI app builder
question_text: A business analyst (non-developer) wants to create a custom GenAI application using the company's Q Business index — for example a meeting summary generator — without writing any code. Which Amazon Q capability is designed for this?

options.text: Amazon Q Apps — allows non-developers to build custom GenAI apps from templates using the Q Business index, no code required
Amazon Q Developer — helps developers write and debug code
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows — a visual workflow builder for technical users
AWS Amplify — a full-stack framework requiring front-end development skills

explanation: Amazon Q Apps enables non-technical business users to create purpose-built GenAI apps using templates on top of their Q Business knowledge index, without writing code. Q Developer targets software developers. Bedrock Prompt Flows is visual but targets technical GenAI builders. Amplify requires front-end development skills.
source_topic: Amazon Q Apps, low-code GenAI, Q Business
